This document runs the housing + transportation (H+T) income-share workflow end to end and
shows the checks that matter at each stage. It replaces the main-branch
`Process-GPI-TDM-HT-by-City.ipynb` notebook. All analysis logic lives in
`src/regional_metrics/` (`acs_panel.py`, `ht_income.py`, `pipeline_ht_income.py`); this file
only calls it and inspects the results.

**Metric.** For each city and H+T year,

$$
\text{HPLUST}_{y} = \frac{\text{HTCOST}_{y} \times 12}{\text{MEDINC}_{y,\text{county}}}
$$

where `HTCOST` is the monthly housing + transportation cost and `MEDINC_CNTY` is the ACS 5-year
county median household income (`B19013_001E`) of the city's county. It is a 0--1 annual share.

**Run it** with the project environment (no separate kernel is registered; Quarto uses the
`python3` kernel inside the uv-managed `.venv`):

```bash
uv run quarto render analysis/ht-income.qmd
```

## Setup

The Census API key is read from `CENSUS_API_KEY` in the environment or `.env`. It is only
needed when a cache is missing or stale; delete a cached panel (or pass `refresh=True`) to
force a re-download.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

from regional_metrics.pipeline_ht_income import (
    build_ht_income,
    validate_against_baseline,
    write_ht_income_outputs,
)
from regional_metrics.settings import load_census_api_key, load_ht_income_config

pd.options.display.max_columns = None
pd.options.display.width = 140

config = load_ht_income_config()

try:
    api_key = load_census_api_key()
except RuntimeError:
    api_key = None  # fine when every cache is already present

api_key is not None
```

## Run the workflow

```{python}
result = build_ht_income(config, api_key)

print("H+T years :", result.target_years)
print(f"ACS years : {result.acs_years[0]}-{result.acs_years[-1]}")
print("Export    :", result.export.shape, "| CRS", result.export.crs.to_epsg())
```

## Input checks

Cities in the cost CSV must all exist in the city layer. Layer-only rows are geometry with no
H+T costs (non-residential TDM zones such as Utah Lake or Camp Williams).

```{python}
result.name_mismatches
```

## Block-group income provenance

Block-group income comes from the ACS where published. Block groups are missing for years
before 2013 (the API does not serve them) and for 2020-vintage block groups before 2020, so
gaps are interpolated or extrapolated. Anything still null falls back to the parent tract,
then the parent county.

```{python}
provenance = (
    result.bg_panel.groupby(["year", "income_source"], dropna=False)
    .size()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
)
provenance
```

```{python}
result.fallback_summary
```

`still_null` should be zero in every year; if not, a block group has no usable income at any
level and its city loses that block group's households from the weighted mean.

## Block groups to cities

Each block group is assigned to the city polygon that contains its centroid, replacing
ArcGIS's `HAVE_THEIR_CENTER_IN`. Unmatched block groups are expected only in non-residential
zones.

```{python}
lookup = result.bg_city_lookup
pd.Series(
    {
        "block groups": len(lookup),
        "matched to a city": int(lookup[config.city_key].notna().sum()),
        "unmatched": int(lookup[config.city_key].isna().sum()),
        "duplicate GEOIDs": int(lookup[config.bg_key].duplicated().sum()),
    }
)
```

## City median income source

`MEDINC{year}_CITY` uses the ACS Place value where a city matches a Census Place, the ACS
county value for whole-county TDM rows, and the household-weighted block-group mean
otherwise. The table shows which source each city resolved to in the latest ACS year.

```{python}
result.medinc_sources["medinc_source"].value_counts().rename("cities").to_frame()
```

## HPLUST by year

```{python}
share_columns = [f"HPLUST{year}" for year in result.target_years]
export = pd.DataFrame(result.export.drop(columns=result.export.geometry.name))
export[share_columns].replace(0, float("nan")).describe().T[["count", "min", "50%", "max"]]
```

Zeros are the legacy placeholder for "no county income"; they are excluded above. Expected
range is roughly 0--0.6. A maximum above 1 would indicate a calculation error.

```{python}
assert (export[share_columns].max() < 1).all(), "HPLUST above 1 - check the inputs"
```

### Spot check

One city, end to end, so the arithmetic can be verified by hand:

```{python}
year = result.target_years[-1]
row = export.loc[export[config.city_key] == "Alpine"].iloc[0]
pd.Series(
    {
        "HCOST (monthly)": row[f"HCOST{year}"],
        "TCOST (monthly)": row[f"TCOST{year}"],
        "HTCOST (monthly)": row[f"HTCOST{year}"],
        "MEDINC_CNTY": row[f"MEDINC{year}_CNTY"],
        "HPLUST": row[f"HPLUST{year}"],
        "check: HTCOST*12/MEDINC_CNTY": row[f"HTCOST{year}"] * 12 / row[f"MEDINC{year}_CNTY"],
    },
    name=f"Alpine {year}",
)
```

## Parity with the main branch

The result is compared with the snapshot exported from the main-branch notebook (see
`baseline_csv` in `config/ht_income.yml`). Income and share columns must match exactly;
`TOTPOP` / `TOTHH` allow a small tolerance (see the config comment).

```{python}
report = validate_against_baseline(result.export, config)

print("Parity passed          :", report.passed)
print("Same column order      :", report.column_order_matches)
print("Missing / extra columns:", report.missing_columns, report.extra_columns)
print("Missing / extra cities :", report.missing_keys, report.extra_keys)
report.column_diffs.sort_values("max_abs_diff", ascending=False).head(10)
```

```{python}
assert report.passed, report.failing_columns
```
